43_marg2872: The vision of Obadiah. Obadiah, the shorter, the deeper, means “servant of God,” as Moses is called the servant of God and the Apostle the servant of Christ; and he saw and heard things worthy of a prophet's service. This, then, is the vision of Obadiah, which he sees among the nations to which the Lord sent an ambassador; for the destruction of Edom is a vision of the nations. And though “vision” is put in the title, he does not go on to say that he saw anything, only that he heard. So “vision” is put here for understanding, after the manner of the prophets, who understand what they see and hear; from this vision the prophets are called seers. A great part of this prophecy is contained in the book of Jeremiah, with some words changed.
43_marg2873: Esau, son of Isaac, brother of Jacob, was also called Edom, that is, “red,” and Seir, that is, “hairy.” He possessed the region that is now called Gebalena, where the Horites lived before, whose name means “free men.” The city that is called Edom in Hebrew and Idumea in Greek, from the name of its founder, is a small town of Palestine, to which it is said through Amos: “For three crimes of Edom, and for four I will not convert him.” So as the same man is called by three names, so his land too is called Edom, Idumea and Seir. This region is not counted among the foreign nations, because it was possessed by the son of Isaac, the brother of Jacob; nor was it given to the children of Israel as a possession, but the children of Israel were forbidden to take up arms against their brother. But as Esau out of hatred persecuted his brother Jacob, so the Edomites were always enemies to the Israelites. So it is against the Edomites that this prophet speaks.
43_marg2874: According to the history: O Edom, though you are the least compared with the other nations round about, you are lifted up in pride; and though you are contemptible and poor, having no roofed buildings but living in caves, you are raised on high like an eagle, and so swollen in heart that you believe you dwell among the stars and bring all nations under your rule.
43_marg2875: According to the moral sense, the word is spoken against the carnal Jews, who envy the Christians and persecute Jacob their brother, that is, the people of the supplanter, who snatched the birthright from them. Or it is spoken against the heretics, who, while they seem to be our neighbours, are our opponents, and strive to drive the simple dweller out of his father's inheritance. Or against the world, which is earthly and bloody; hence Isaias: “Who is this that cometh from Edom, with dyed garments from Bosra?” Some understand by Edom the flesh, against whose assault they think the soul is called out, so that, having mortified our “members which are upon the earth,” we may attain eternal glory in Christ. The Jews dream in vain that this prophecy is aimed at the Roman empire.

43_marg2877: Allegorically. 43_marg2904: And the captivity of this host. Allegorically. Sarepta means “narrowness of bread,” or “burning”; Chanaan, “movement,” or “merchant,” or “humble.” When the captivity of the children of Israel, leaving the letter that killeth, comes to the spirit that quickeneth, it will set in motion all that belongs to the law, and, made humble, will trade many pearls for one; and where there was once a scarcity of bread, it will give food, and will burn up the vices. And the captivity of Jerusalem, where once was the vision of peace, now spread through the whole world, will possess the churches of the true light. And then the saviours, the apostles, chosen from the remnant of the Jews, will go up to the watchtower of the mountain of the Church, and, putting down the pride of the Jews and of all the mountains that lift themselves up against the knowledge of God, will prepare the kingdom for the Lord.
